## Summary

Created `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/concurrent/EventCountCircuitBreakerAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering:

- All three constructors and their threshold/interval getters (including unit conversion to nanoseconds)
- Initial `closed` state per the class-level contract
- `checkState()`/`incrementAndCheckState()` happy path, with the invariant that the boolean return always matches `isClosed()`
- Negative increment rejection (`IllegalArgumentException`) and zero/large increments not throwing
- Manual `open()`/`close()` transitions and their documented no-op idempotency when already in that state
- `addChangeListener`/`removeChangeListener`/`PROPERTY_NAME`, verifying notifications fire only on real transitions (not on no-op calls), based on the "notified whenever a state transition occurs" contract
- `nanoTime()` sanity-checked against `System.nanoTime()`
- Deterministic open→close lifecycle driven by interval boundaries, using a same-package subclass that overrides the package-private `nanoTime()` hook to control time without any timing flakiness

Where the javadoc was ambiguous about fine-grained timing semantics (e.g., whether a single call's own increment counts toward the interval being evaluated), I designed assertions with enough margin to hold under either reasonable reading of the contract, rather than asserting an unverifiable implementation detail.
